_about: What llm-launch gives opencode in its sessions: the tested plugin sets (setups, with their options) and the opencode settings.
A new tested setup is an edit here plus a push; llm-launch offers the update at its next start on each machine.
setup_version: raise it when setup.sh gains a step every machine must run (a new llama.cpp build, say); opencode: the
version these plugins were tested with. After an update, the launcher offers to run setup.sh when either one moved on.
setups: the first with default true is used unless the person turns another on; every other setup is a yes / no
question at each start (its 'ask' text), the answer remembered. 'setup' (top level) is the default setup's name.
Plugin source: 'file' = a file in this repo (with 'sha256': it must match), or 'url' + 'sha256' = downloaded once into
~/.config/llm-launch/plugins/ (kept only if the checksum matches). In option values, {kit} is this folder and {state}
is ~/.config/llm-launch. A replacement system prompt is a text file in prompts/, passed to plugins/system-prompt.js as
its 'file' option (used exactly as it is: no trailing newline; 'prompt_sha256' pins it). A changed prompt text gets a
new file name, so each session can be matched to the tested setup it ran.
Only one plugin may replace opencode's own prompt (compaction-anchor's slim part or system-prompt.js), and only one may
replace the turn after a summary (system-prompt.js continueText, compaction-anchor's no-stop-and-ask, or a task driver,
which handles that turn itself); a task driver runs without the compaction-anchor parts. check-kit.py enforces these.
interaction-mode.js (marked "untested": true) rides along in every setup, after system-prompt.js: in autonomous mode (the default
here, the tested one) it changes nothing the model sees; plan-first and interactive (untested) replace the prompt's Questions
section. The launcher asks at each start which mode to start in and passes it as the plugin's 'default'.
Before pushing a change here: python3 check-kit.py --fetch
